clue.text: A learner, one getting second grade, is offering excuses

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate letter
I is the Roman numeral for one
B is the grade after A, the second mark in school grading
taken as written

explanation.surface: A student driver, having scraped a B grade, comes up with reasons for failing.
explanation.definitionFit: Alibis are pleas or justifications offered to dodge blame, so they serve as reasons a person gives.

clue.text: Heather's weird topless — get her this quick!

parts.note: ling is another name for heather, the moorland shrub

indicators.note: topless means the top, here the first letter, of the synonym for weird is cut off

parts.note: weird means eerie

explanation.surface: A man urged to buy a racy present quickly, with an odd aside about someone called Heather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes the first letter of EERIE, leaving ERIE. Heather looks like a woman's name, but it is the plant, LING.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingerie is women's underwear, the classic gift a man hurries to buy for his partner.

clue.text: Soluble preparation getting black in each tub shifted

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: shifted means the letters of 'each tub' are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: Something dissolving and black-tinted appearing as each bath is moved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifted' rearranges EACH TUB into ATHCUBE, which follows B.
explanation.definitionFit: A bath cube is a small block of scented salts that dissolves in bathwater, a soluble toiletry.

clue.text: Reserve position or principal part?

parts.note: a sub, short for substitute, is a reserve player
a stance is a position or posture

explanation.surface: A question about whether a substitute player's place is the main role.
explanation.definitionFit: The substance of something is its essence or main body, the most important portion.

clue.text: Army chief at home fooling

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
a king is a chief or ruler
in means at home, as in 'staying in'

explanation.surface: A senior military commander relaxing at home and playing practical jokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking someone in means deceiving or hoodwinking them, as fooling does.

clue.text: Young criminal can trick older, dafter thug

indicators.note: trick suggests the letters of 'older, dafter thug' are played about with and rearranged

explanation.surface: A young offender can outwit an older but stupider thug.
explanation.walkthrough: The fifteen letters of OLDER DAFTER THUG are rearranged. The Artful Dodger is the boy pickpocket in Dickens's Oliver Twist.
explanation.definitionFit: The Artful Dodger is Dickens's juvenile pickpocket in Fagin's gang, a youthful offender.

clue.text: I am to suffer or get better

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
prove in its old sense means to undergo or experience, so to suffer

explanation.surface: Someone resigned to pain or recovery, one or the other.
explanation.walkthrough: PROVE here is the archaic sense of experiencing or undergoing something, as in proving hardship.
explanation.definitionFit: To improve is to become better in health or quality, to make progress.

clue.text: Legs said to be wonky in dancing movement

indicators.note: wonky means crooked or awry, so the letters of 'legs said' are set askew into a new order

explanation.surface: A dancer's legs are reportedly unsteady during a step.
explanation.definitionFit: A glissade is a ballet step, a gliding move from one foot to the other.

clue.text: Oughtn't I somehow to get an evening's entertainment?

indicators.note: somehow implies the letters of 'Oughtn't I' are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: Someone wondering whether they should treat themselves to a bit of fun.
explanation.definitionFit: A night out is an evening spent socialising away from home, at a pub, show or restaurant.

clue.text: A French farm building likely to collapse

parts.note: un is French for a
a stable is a farm building for horses

explanation.surface: A rickety French barn about to fall down.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unstable is unsteady and liable to topple or give way.

clue.text: It's bound to be a feel-good time?

explanation.surface: A teasing guess that cheerfulness is inevitable.
explanation.walkthrough: To spring is to leap, so a spring is a bound; a coiled spring is also wound and held tight.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring is a leap or jump; the season of renewal after winter lifts the mood.

clue.text: Map-maker in German car by a hill

parts.note: a Merc is a Mercedes, a German make of car
a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A cartographer sitting in a Mercedes next to a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: Mercator was the Flemish cartographer whose projection is used for many world maps.
explanation.definitionFit: Gerardus Mercator was a sixteenth-century cartographer famous for his projection of the globe.

clue.text: Pamper officer's clique

parts.note: CO is commanding officer, so CO's is the officer's
a set is a clique or social circle

explanation.surface: Indulging the commanding officer's inner circle.
explanation.definitionFit: To cosset is to coddle or spoil someone with excessive care.

clue.text: A fib once destroyed a holy man

indicators.note: destroyed means the letters of 'a fib once' are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A small lie once brought down a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' rearranges AFIBONCE. St Boniface was the English missionary to Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Boniface was an eighth-century missionary bishop venerated as a saint.

clue.text: Youngster noted in church?

parts.note: noted suggests famous, but it means singing notes: a young singer in a church choir

explanation.surface: A child who became famous at church.
explanation.definitionFit: A chorister is a member of a choir, often a boy singing in a cathedral.

clue.text: Dole enables male to take summer abroad

parts.note: ete is French for summer

explanation.surface: Unemployment benefit lets a man spend the summer overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dole' looks like a noun, unemployment benefit, but here it is the verb to share out.
explanation.definitionFit: To mete out is to allot or distribute portions, just as one doles things out.

clue.text: Meal lists including beer brought up for old king

indicators.note: including means the menus hold another piece within them

parts.note: menus are lists of dishes for a meal

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means the word for beer is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: ale is beer

explanation.surface: Restaurant menus with beer, served up to an ancient monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' turns ALE into ELA, which 'including' puts inside MENUS. Menelaus was king of Sparta, husband of Helen of Troy.
explanation.definitionFit: Menelaus was the legendary Spartan king whose wife Helen was taken to Troy.

clue.text: Showing discernment, set fault out

indicators.note: out means the letters of 'set fault' are thrown out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A critic with good judgement points out a defect.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasteful means displaying good aesthetic judgement and refinement.

clue.text: Beastly home in home counties permitting no booze

parts.note: the home counties surround London in the south-east of England, SE
TT means teetotal, drinking no alcohol

explanation.surface: An animal's house in a dry part of the south of England.
explanation.walkthrough: The home counties are the English counties around London, so SE (south-east).
explanation.definitionFit: A sett is the burrow of a badger, an animal's dwelling.

clue.text: Bygone period when one would get into a coach

indicators.note: get into means one piece goes inside the word for the coach

parts.note: a stage, short for stagecoach, is a horse-drawn coach
taken as written

explanation.surface: Recalling an era when a traveller boarded a horse-drawn carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stone Age is the prehistoric era when tools were made of flint.

clue.text: Conservative showing regret after time, sad

indicators.note: after places the word for regret following the letter for time

parts.note: to rue is to regret
blue means sad or low

explanation.surface: A Tory politician full of sorrowful remorse after a while.
explanation.walkthrough: A true blue is a staunch Conservative, blue being the British Conservative Party's colour.
explanation.definitionFit: True blue describes a loyal, staunch Tory, blue being that party's colour.

clue.text: Wood dodgy salesman distributed

parts.note: deal is pine or fir timber
a tout sells tickets at inflated prices, a shady seller

explanation.surface: A shady timber trader handed out his goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Dealt out means handed round or shared among people, as cards are.

clue.text: Richard to avoid sound style

indicators.note: sound tells us the words for Richard and avoid are said aloud, giving a word that sounds alike

parts.note: Dick is short for Richard, and to shun is to avoid

explanation.surface: A man named Richard avoiding a sensible manner of doing things.
explanation.walkthrough: DICK + SHUN, spoken, sounds like the answer. 'sound' looks like an adjective on style but signals the homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: Diction is a style of speaking or writing, the choice and delivery of words.

clue.text: Tempt part of hospital to take illegal drug

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
ice is slang for crystal methamphetamine

explanation.surface: A hospital department being lured into taking narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: To entice is to lure or attract someone with a promise of pleasure.

clue.text: One tried with difficulty to get properly into line

indicators.note: with difficulty suggests the letters of 'one tried' are wrestled into another order

explanation.surface: Someone struggles to get everything neatly lined up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something oriented is aligned or positioned correctly in relation to its surroundings.

clue.text: Business relationship from which spouse is excluded

definitions.text: relationship from which spouse is excluded

explanation.surface: A firm's dealings that leave a wife or husband out.
explanation.definitionFit: An affair is a matter or concern; it is also a secret romance kept from one's husband or wife.

clue.text: Instruction to acquire item of furniture that's available

parts.note: get is an order to obtain something
a table is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: An order to buy a piece of furniture that is on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gettable means obtainable or within reach.

clue.text: Description of maverick group that gets under your skin?

explanation.surface: A rebel faction that irritates people.
explanation.definitionFit: A splinter group breaks away from a larger party; a splinter is also a sliver of wood lodged in flesh.

clue.text: Jim no longer with us old magistrates

explanation.surface: The late Jim alongside former local officials.
explanation.walkthrough: Jim Reeves was an American country singer who died in 1964. Reeves were medieval English local officials.
explanation.definitionFit: Jim Reeves is a deceased country star; reeves were chief officers of a town or district in Anglo-Saxon England.
